Proxys.io is the better choice when you want a few fixed IPs per account at the lowest cost, unlimited bandwidth on dedicated addresses, cheap bulk IPv6 or flat-rate mobile proxies, with a 24-hour refund window. Heavy-bandwidth account work often favours Proxys.io's flat pricing.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven is the quality-first option. Instead of handing out whatever IP the pool returns, it screens addresses in real time and lets you choose how strict the screening is. That matters most for account-based work such as social media management and multi-accounting, where a flagged IP can cost you an account. The price reflects it: $4.50/GB without a plan and $2.20/GB on monthly plans.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs Proxys.io

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; NodeMaven comes to about $45. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; NodeMaven comes to about $220. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while Proxys.io's does not (rental periods (days or months)), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. NodeMaven lists '30M+ residential + 250K mobile' and Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: compare the exact target and traffic plan before choosing. PROXYS.IO reports a 100M+ rotating residential network across 195 countries, in addition to static rentals. Pool size alone does not establish success rate; this brief does not independently benchmark PROXYS.IO against the other provider.

SERP and rank tracking: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need. With Proxys.io: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. With Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. Run the same small test on both before committing.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: fine for light checks. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: good quality but a smaller pool. How Proxys.io compares: limited geo depth.
Tight budgets: Proxys.io. Proxys.io has the edge here. Why: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. How NodeMaven compares: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and Proxys.io before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle NodeMaven vs Proxys.io faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 3, Proxys.io in 1, and 2 are ties. That makes NodeMaven the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
